name: HubSpot
summary: CRM platform with marketing, sales, service and content hubs on one contact database.
best_for: teams that want marketing, sales, service and content on one contact database and will actually use more than one hub: that shared database is the real product, and it is what makes the price defensible when you use the breadth
skip_if: you need one job done well and cheaply, because a dedicated tool will almost always beat the equivalent HubSpot hub on price; or your contact list is growing fast and your budget is not, since contacts are the meter that moves without you touching anything
honest_knock:
Three numbers on this pricing page are not what they look like, and they compound.

The first is the $7. It is the number in large black type on the Starter card, and the $20 beside it in small grey type is the list price. The banner above the table explains why: up to 65% off Starter, new customers only, for a limited time. So $7 is an introductory rate and $20 is what the seat costs afterwards: a 186% step for a system that by then holds your contact database, which is the single most painful kind of software to leave.

The second is the $800. Professional carries a required one-time onboarding fee of $3,000, disclosed in a footnote under the card rather than in the price. Year one on Professional is therefore $800 × 12 + $3,000 = $12,600 if you pay annually, or $890 × 12 + $3,000 = $13,680 if you pay monthly on an annual commitment (pricing page, 28 Nov 2026). The onboarding adds roughly a third to the first year, and no amount of shopping around removes it: it is mandatory. Enterprise does the same thing at $7,000 on top of $43,200 a year.

The third is the seat count, because it is not the meter that usually bites. Professional includes 3 Core Seats and 2,000 marketing contacts. For a marketing platform, contacts are the axis that grows on its own: your list gets bigger whether or not you hire anyone, and the contact tier moves the bill without anyone deciding to upgrade. Price your next two years on the list you expect to have, not the team you have now.

One more thing worth knowing before you start on Free. The free tier is usable (two users, 1,000 contacts, no expiry) and that is exactly how the ladder is designed to work. The step from Starter to Professional is not incremental: at list prices a three-seat team goes from $60 a month to $890 plus $3,000 once, which is roughly fifteen times the monthly cost. Whatever you build on Free, build it knowing where the next rung is.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Starter, per seat · the list price per seat per month
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-09 in a live browser on their own marketing and CRM pricing pages, USD view; first read 2026-08-18, no amount changed in between) Free is $0 for up to 2 users and 1,000 marketing contacts, with no time limit. Starter is advertised at $7 per seat a month against a list price of $20 per seat a month, under a banner reading “Save up to 65% on Starter — new customers only, select offers available for a limited time”. It includes 500 HubSpot Credits and 1,000 marketing contacts. Professional starts at $800 a month paid annually, or $890 a month billed monthly, and includes 3 Core Seats with additional Core Seats from $45 a month, 3,000 credits and 2,000 marketing contacts. On top of that comes a required one-time Professional Onboarding fee of $3,000 that the headline price does not include. Enterprise starts at $3,600 a month with 5 Core Seats, extra seats from $75, 5,000 credits and 10,000 marketing contacts, and a required one-time onboarding fee of $7,000. HubSpot AEO, their answer-engine visibility tracker, is sold separately at $50 a month or $45 annually for 25 prompts across 3 engines, with a 28-day trial; on the 9 October reading the page adds that AEO is also included in Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise. The Free Tools FAQ caps a free account at 1,000 contacts, 2 users and 1,000 records across the other standard object types.

compare_with.name: Pipedrive or Close
compare_with.why: the honest comparison is not feature-for-feature but shape-for-shape. Pipedrive and Close are sales tools that do one job and publish a per-seat price you can multiply in your head. HubSpot is a database with hubs bolted around it, priced on two meters at once (seats and contacts) with a mandatory onboarding fee at the Professional rung. If you want a CRM, the dedicated tools are cheaper and simpler. If you want marketing, sales and service reading from one contact record, that is the thing HubSpot sells and they do not really compete. Verify all current price lists yourself; ours were read on 18 August 2026.

claims.claim: Small teams with fewer than 1,000 contacts
claims.observed: Three test contacts were imported through a quick import and a pipeline, a deal and a form were made. The free plan shows Up to 2 users; the dossier limit of 1,000 contacts was not seen and not tested, and nothing with a real list of contacts was done.
claims.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought
claims.comparability: The dossier audience against a test with 3 test contacts; no contact limit was reached or shown.
claims.buying_consequence: The test shows that a small team can start on the free plan; whether 1,000 contacts is the limit was not seen.

claims.claim: Teams about to outgrow the free plan
claims.observed: The free plan says Up to 2 users, and the locks that were seen are Upgrade to Data Hub, Prospecting Agent and Workflows with an upgrade icon. The Starter offer card says Save up to 65% on Starter with 1 seat at $7 a month.
claims.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought
claims.comparability: The upgrade icons and the offer card against the dossier audience; no plan was bought.
claims.buying_consequence: You hit the limits of the free plan quickly in the places where it locks features, and the app pushes Starter at once.

claims.observed: The offer card in Account and Billing says Save up to 65% on Starter and the plans page says Limited-time, 65% off at 7 euro a month per seat billed annually. The promotion is confirmed, but no list price for Starter is shown on that page.
claims.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought
claims.comparability: The offer card and the annual view of the plans page against the dossier promotion; no checkout total was seen.
claims.buying_consequence: The Starter promotion exists and is described as limited-time; what the seat costs afterwards is not shown in the app.

claims.observed: With the switch on Billed monthly the plans page shows Starter with Limited-time, 50% off at 10 euro a month per seat. A list price for Starter appears nowhere on the page, while the dossier says $20 per seat a month at list.
claims.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought
claims.comparability: The monthly view of the plans page against the dossier list price; the currency differs and no list price is shown.
claims.buying_consequence: The monthly price after the promotion cannot be read in the app view, so check the list price before you rely on the offer.

claims.observed: The plans page shows Professional at 90 euro a month per seat billed annually, 100 euro billed monthly, and Enterprise at 175 euro per seat. The dossier gives $800 a month paid annually or $890 a month for 3 seats and $3,600 for Enterprise, in US dollars.
claims.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought
claims.comparability: The euro per-seat view of the plans page against the dossier prices in dollars for a seat bundle.
claims.buying_consequence: The app view counts per seat in euro and the dossier counts a bundle of seats in dollars, so the two cannot be set side by side without a conversion.

claims.claim: Starter plans are not required to purchase onboarding.
claims.observed: The FAQ says that Professional or Enterprise plans are required to purchase onboarding and that Starter plans are not. The amount of the onboarding is not shown, while the dossier names a required fee of $3,000 for Professional.
claims.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought
claims.comparability: The FAQ text against the dossier fee; no amount was visible to compare.
claims.buying_consequence: The mandatory onboarding fee of Professional is mentioned but its amount is not shown in the app view, so ask for it in writing.

claims.observed: The plans page lists credits a month: Starter 5,000, Professional 10,000 and Enterprise 15,000. The dossier names a lower number of credits for each paid plan.
claims.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought
claims.comparability: The credits row of the plans page against the dossier credit numbers.
claims.buying_consequence: The paid plans show more credits a month in the app than the dossier says.

claims.observed: Starter allows Up to 10 users and the free plan Up to 2 users, with extra seats at the Professional and Enterprise prices per seat. The dossier gives 2 users for the free plan, which matches.
claims.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session set up the free HubSpot CRM, imported 3 test contacts, made a test deal and an empty form, and read the plans up to the Starter checkout. The interface had to be switched from Dutch to English first (about 3 minutes); after that the wizard gave a usable pipeline of 8 stages in about 4 minutes from the start and the test deal took 3 steps. The import asked for a legal basis. The free plan shows Up to 2 users, HubSpot branding on the form and on e-mails, and upgrade locks on Data Hub, Prospecting Agent and Workflows. The wizard says that it added Gmail and Google Calendar although nothing was connected. The public dollar page still shows the dossier prices (Starter $7 against a list price of $20, Professional $800 or $890 with a $3,000 onboarding), but the euro per-seat view inside the app shows Starter at 7 euro (65% off) or 10 euro (50% off) without a list price and Professional at 90 or 100 euro per seat. Tax and the total were not seen and nothing was bought or deleted. Account and start: the account (the free CRM, region eu1) was created by us and was signed in in his Chrome; our AI assistant ran the test from 15:12 (Amsterdam). The dossier name is HubSpot and the review is on MSS (mss/hubspot-review.html). The audiences from the dossier: Small teams with fewer than 1,000 contacts, Teams about to outgrow the free plan, and Sales teams that only need a lead pipeline (the dossier names noCRM as the alternative). Language: the interface was in Dutch and the address trick with lang=en did not help. The language was changed under the user preferences, General, Language, from Dutch to English and saved; the app said that it takes a few minutes. After about 3 minutes the wizard was in English, but the sidebar and the names of the standard views sometimes jumped back to Dutch and the feature lists on the plans page stay partly Dutch. Screenshots were only made of English screens or cropped. Wizard: the AI assistant Set up CRM started again at Step 1 of 6: company details Yes, looks good; goal Track software deals; tools: five tools (an e-mail inbox, a calendar, Outlook, a WordPress plug-in and a sales navigator) were switched on by default and all five were unticked before I'm done selecting my tools. Deviation: the closing sentence of the wizard still says that it added tools like Gmail and Google Calendar, but nothing was connected (the banner to connect the inbox was still there). The dashboard step was skipped (Skip this). The wizard was done at about 15:16. Core action: wizard step 5, Track your deal progress, offered a Deal pipeline with 8 deal stages (Lead Identified, Initial Outreach, Needs Assessment, Demo Scheduled, Proposal Sent, Negotiation and more) with the button Use this pipeline. The result is the pipeline AI Tool Sales Pipeline with a sample deal HubSpot - New Deal (Sample Deal). Time to the first usable pipeline: about 4 minutes from the start, about 2 minutes in the wizard itself. Test deal: Deals, Add deals, Create new, name Test Deal Acme, amount 500, stage Lead Identified, Create: 3 steps, about 15:16 to 15:17. The deal record shows our name as owner (not used on the screenshots; masked on the board screenshot). Import: Data integration, Import data, Quick import (Contacts only), a test file test-contacten-3.csv of 210 bytes added through the file field. Step 2 Match your data to our contact properties: First Name, Last Name and Email all Mapped. Step 3 requires Select the legal basis for processing a contact's data; Legitimate interest - Lead was chosen. Finish import at 15:17. Result: 3 contacts (Test Lead01 to 03, test01 to 03 at example.com, primary company example.com); the page first showed dashes and after a reload 5 contacts (with 2 sample contacts of HubSpot). Form: Forms, Create form, Start from blank. The editor says Saved with unpublished changes and has the text We'd love to hear from you!, the fields First Name, Last Name and Email and the button Submit; under the form: Create your own free forms to generate leads from your website. (HubSpot branding on the free form). Not published and not embedded. Limits of the free plan: Data integration shows Upgrade to Data Hub with a lock at Make sense of intent data; the account says Free, Up to 2 users; the plans table lists Up to 2 users, 2000 sent e-mails per calendar month with HubSpot branding, 100 active and 100 static segments, 1 blog with HubSpot branding, live chat with HubSpot branding, a maximum of 1 personal meeting link and 3 connected ad accounts. The left navigation has the buttons Upgrade to Starter and Prospecting Agent and Workflows with an upgrade icon. Plans up to the payment: Read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 in the app and on the public plans page, in the euro view (Billed annually and Billed monthly). Free: 0 euro a month, No credit card required, Up to 2 users, 2000 sent e-mails per calendar month with HubSpot branding, 100 active and 100 static segments, 1 blog with HubSpot branding. Starter: Limited-time 65% off, 7 euro a month per seat when billed annually; Limited-time 50% off, 10 euro a month per seat when billed monthly; no list price is shown; Up to 10 users; 5,000 credits a month. Inside the app the offer card says Save up to 65% on Starter, GTM Seat (Starter), 1 seat - $7/mo. Professional: 90 euro a month per seat billed annually or 100 euro billed monthly, 10,000 credits a month. Enterprise: 175 euro a month per seat, 15,000 credits a month. The FAQ says that Professional or Enterprise plans are required to purchase onboarding and that Starter plans are not; the amount of the onboarding is not shown. Buy now on Starter opened Configure Your Plan (Buy Starter, GTM Seats 10 euro a month, 5,000 credits a month, Est. monthly billing 10 euro a month) and Continue to checkout, which asked for the company details that are used to calculate tax; the tax and the total only appear after those are filled in, which was not done, so they were not seen. The checkout was left through the address bar and nothing was bought. The public US dollar pricing pages hubspot.com/pricing and hubspot.com/pricing/crm were read again just before this delivery on the same day: Starter $7 a month per seat against a struck through $20 a month per seat with 500 HubSpot Credits and 1,000 marketing contacts, Professional starts at $800 a month paid annually or $890 a month billed monthly with 3 Core Seats and a required one-time onboarding of $3,000, Enterprise starts at $3,600 a month with a required onboarding of $7,000, and Free is $0 for up to 2 users. The dossier prices are therefore UNCHANGED on the public page. Deviations: (1) the euro per-seat view inside the app and on the plans page that the tester saw shows Professional at 90 or 100 euro per seat and Enterprise at 175 euro per seat and no list price for Starter, while the dossier and the public dollar page show $800 or $890 for 3 seats, $3,600 and a $20 list price for Starter; the two views differ in currency and in how the seats are counted, so they are not comparable one to one. (2) The onboarding amount ($3,000) is not shown in the app view, only the rule that Professional and Enterprise must buy it. (3) Starter credits are 5,000 a month in the app against 500 in the dossier and on the public dollar page. (4) The dossier says the Free plan holds 1,000 marketing contacts; the plans page of the app mentions Up to 2 users and an e-mail limit of 2000 a month, and no contact limit was seen. Cancelling: Account and Billing, Delete account, Delete Your HubSpot Account: the hub and all content associated with it will be deleted, and the note says that this will not automatically delete the associated user profiles. The red button Delete account was not clicked. There is no paid plan to downgrade; the free plan stays. Not tested: connecting a mailbox or calendar and the e-mail history on a contact, publishing or embedding the form, inviting a second user, a Starter trial or payment, the tax amount in the checkout, the onboarding amount of Professional, workflows and sequences. Clean up: the account stays; our language is now English (not set back); the test data stays (contacts Test Lead01 to 03, the deal Test Deal Acme, an empty draft form, the import name, the pipeline and the sample contacts and deal of HubSpot); no mailbox, calendar or integration was connected; our tab was closed, an older wizard our tab was outside our tab group and could not be closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The interface starts in the language of the browser or region and the switch to English takes about 3 minutes, with some parts jumping back to Dutch. The setup wizard switches five tools on by default and its closing sentence says that it added Gmail and Google Calendar although nothing was connected. The import forces a legal basis choice. The free form and the free e-mails carry HubSpot branding, and Data Hub, Prospecting Agent and Workflows are locked. The app shows per-seat prices in euro without a Starter list price and without the onboarding amount, while the public dollar page shows a list price of $20 and an onboarding of $3,000.

claim_checks.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought
claim_checks.comparability: The dossier audience against a test with 3 test contacts; no contact limit was reached or shown.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The test shows that a small team can start on the free plan; whether 1,000 contacts is the limit was not seen.

claim_checks.claim: Teams about to outgrow the free plan

claim_checks.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought
claim_checks.comparability: The upgrade icons and the offer card against the dossier audience; no plan was bought.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: You hit the limits of the free plan quickly in the places where it locks features, and the app pushes Starter at once.

claim_checks.observed: The offer card in Account and Billing says Save up to 65% on Starter and the plans page says Limited-time, 65% off at 7 euro a month per seat billed annually. The promotion is confirmed, but no list price for Starter is shown on that page.
claim_checks.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought
claim_checks.comparability: The offer card and the annual view of the plans page against the dossier promotion; no checkout total was seen.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The Starter promotion exists and is described as limited-time; what the seat costs afterwards is not shown in the app.

claim_checks.observed: With the switch on Billed monthly the plans page shows Starter with Limited-time, 50% off at 10 euro a month per seat. A list price for Starter appears nowhere on the page, while the dossier says $20 per seat a month at list.
claim_checks.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought
claim_checks.comparability: The monthly view of the plans page against the dossier list price; the currency differs and no list price is shown.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The monthly price after the promotion cannot be read in the app view, so check the list price before you rely on the offer.

claim_checks.observed: The plans page shows Professional at 90 euro a month per seat billed annually, 100 euro billed monthly, and Enterprise at 175 euro per seat. The dossier gives $800 a month paid annually or $890 a month for 3 seats and $3,600 for Enterprise, in US dollars.
claim_checks.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought
claim_checks.comparability: The euro per-seat view of the plans page against the dossier prices in dollars for a seat bundle.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The app view counts per seat in euro and the dossier counts a bundle of seats in dollars, so the two cannot be set side by side without a conversion.

claim_checks.claim: Starter plans are not required to purchase onboarding.

claim_checks.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought
claim_checks.comparability: The FAQ text against the dossier fee; no amount was visible to compare.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The mandatory onboarding fee of Professional is mentioned but its amount is not shown in the app view, so ask for it in writing.

claim_checks.observed: The plans page lists credits a month: Starter 5,000, Professional 10,000 and Enterprise 15,000. The dossier names a lower number of credits for each paid plan.
claim_checks.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought
claim_checks.comparability: The credits row of the plans page against the dossier credit numbers.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The paid plans show more credits a month in the app than the dossier says.

claim_checks.observed: Starter allows Up to 10 users and the free plan Up to 2 users, with extra seats at the Professional and Enterprise prices per seat. The dossier gives 2 users for the free plan, which matches.
claim_checks.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought
claim_checks.comparability: The user limits on the plans page and the account card against the dossier limit of 2 users.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The free plan stops at 2 users and Starter at 10.

claim_checks.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought
claim_checks.comparability: The closing sentence of the wizard against the connection banner and the unticked tools.

claim_checks.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought

claim_checks.plan: Free CRM account; a contact import, a deal pipeline, a test deal and an empty form were made and the plans were read up to the company details of the Starter checkout, nothing was bought

Free: 0 euro a month, No credit card required, Up to 2 users, 2000 sent e-mails per calendar month with HubSpot branding, 100 active and 100 static segments, 1 blog with HubSpot branding. Starter: Limited-time 65% off, 7 euro a month per seat when billed annually; Limited-time 50% off, 10 euro a month per seat when billed monthly; no list price is shown; Up to 10 users; 5,000 credits a month. Inside the app the offer card says Save up to 65% on Starter, GTM Seat (Starter), 1 seat - $7/mo. Professional: 90 euro a month per seat billed annually or 100 euro billed monthly, 10,000 credits a month. Enterprise: 175 euro a month per seat, 15,000 credits a month. The FAQ says that Professional or Enterprise plans are required to purchase onboarding and that Starter plans are not; the amount of the onboarding is not shown. Buy now on Starter opened Configure Your Plan (Buy Starter, GTM Seats 10 euro a month, 5,000 credits a month, Est. monthly billing 10 euro a month) and Continue to checkout, which asked for the company details that are used to calculate tax; the tax and the total only appear after those are filled in, which was not done, so they were not seen. The checkout was left through the address bar and nothing was bought. The public US dollar pricing pages hubspot.com/pricing and hubspot.com/pricing/crm were read again just before this delivery on the same day: Starter $7 a month per seat against a struck through $20 a month per seat with 500 HubSpot Credits and 1,000 marketing contacts, Professional starts at $800 a month paid annually or $890 a month billed monthly with 3 Core Seats and a required one-time onboarding of $3,000, Enterprise starts at $3,600 a month with a required onboarding of $7,000, and Free is $0 for up to 2 users. The dossier prices are therefore UNCHANGED on the public page. Deviations: (1) the euro per-seat view inside the app and on the plans page that the tester saw shows Professional at 90 or 100 euro per seat and Enterprise at 175 euro per seat and no list price for Starter, while the dossier and the public dollar page show $800 or $890 for 3 seats, $3,600 and a $20 list price for Starter; the two views differ in currency and in how the seats are counted, so they are not comparable one to one. (2) The onboarding amount ($3,000) is not shown in the app view, only the rule that Professional and Enterprise must buy it. (3) Starter credits are 5,000 a month in the app against 500 in the dossier and on the public dollar page. (4) The dossier says the Free plan holds 1,000 marketing contacts; the plans page of the app mentions Up to 2 users and an e-mail limit of 2000 a month, and no contact limit was seen. Cancelling: Account and Billing, Delete account, Delete Your HubSpot Account: the hub and all content associated with it will be deleted, and the note says that this will not automatically delete the associated user profiles. The red button Delete account was not clicked. There is no paid plan to downgrade; the free plan stays. Not tested: connecting a mailbox or calendar and the e-mail history on a contact, publishing or embedding the form, inviting a second user, a Starter trial or payment, the tax amount in the checkout, the onboarding amount of Professional, workflows and sequences. Clean up: the account stays; our language is now English (not set back); the test data stays (contacts Test Lead01 to 03, the deal Test Deal Acme, an empty draft form, the import name, the pipeline and the sample contacts and deal of HubSpot); no mailbox, calendar or integration was connected; our tab was closed, an older wizard our tab was outside our tab group and could not be closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The interface starts in the language of the browser or region and the switch to English takes about 3 minutes, with some parts jumping back to Dutch. The setup wizard switches five tools on by default and its closing sentence says that it added Gmail and Google Calendar although nothing was connected. The import forces a legal basis choice. The free form and the free e-mails carry HubSpot branding, and Data Hub, Prospecting Agent and Workflows are locked. The app shows per-seat prices in euro without a Starter list price and without the onboarding amount, while the public dollar page shows a list price of $20 and an onboarding of $3,000.

vendor_mcp.what: Two servers. A hosted remote server at mcp.hubspot.com gives any MCP client read and write access to CRM records, marketing and content objects and full activity history over OAuth 2.1 with PKCE; a local Developer MCP server drives the HubSpot Developer Platform through the CLI.
vendor_mcp.plan: Their changelog: the remote server graduated from beta and is "generally available to all HubSpot accounts" as of 13 April 2026. No separate price is named, your existing HubSpot permissions apply, and accounts with sensitive data switched on have activity objects blocked from the server.
vendor_mcp.note: The vendor's own MCP server, from our MCP research; it works with your own account at the vendor.
